01 / THE PACIFIC

A strong signal. Not a local promise.

NOAA’s September 10 discussion reports strengthening El Niño, with a greater than 90% chance of a very strong event during fall and winter 2026–27.

ENSO changes seasonal odds. It cannot identify a California storm eight weeks ahead, and local impacts remain uncertain.

Read the dated NOAA advisory ↗

Latest weekly Niño 3.4 observation: +3.1°C on Sep 23, relative to 1991–2020. This weekly SST anomaly is not ONI. Observed series ↗

02 / BEYOND TWO WEEKS

Watch the probabilities.

Long-range guidance is best read as regional shifts relative to normal, rather than a precise day-by-day forecast.

Inspect full metrics & provenance ↗
WHAT WAS TRAINED

A real, bounded neural pilot.

A CPU-trained residual MLP calibrates CFSv2 ensemble hindcasts against CPC observations from SubseasonalClimateUSA. Features use the model forecast, season and coarse region. Normalization and seasonal climatology fit training data only.

HISTORICAL TRAININGCompleted · seed 42

This is forecast calibration, not a fine-tuned global backbone. The pilot is not applied to the live forecast map.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW

No neural victory lap.

The ridge baseline has lower overall RMSE than the neural model on both variables. A single seed and one held-out period do not establish statistical superiority.

No ENSO-event-independent test, calibrated probabilities, city-level validation, or weeks 5–8 model skill is established. Final revised observations were used; exact historical publication times are not verified.

REPRODUCE & EXTEND

Open the experiment.

Training code, model weights, paired-data provenance and evaluation artifacts are published in the source repository. An ENSO-conditioned PyTorch scaffold remains a separate, unrun extension until historical input vintages are verified.

MODEL TERRAIN & LIMITS

Values below model terrain and outside valid pressure-level brackets are withheld. Profiles can end before the requested 16 days. No extrapolation.

Linear interpolation uses forecast geopotential height. Wind is interpolated as vector components. This is approximate atmospheric guidance, not a terrain-corrected mountain forecast.
